question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=210$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =210\cdot 0.6 \\  & =126 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =210\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =84 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(210)(0.6)=126
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(210)(0.6)(1-0.6)=50.4.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(126,50.4).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(120<X\le 140).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(120<X\le 140)=P(121\le X\le 140)≈P(120.5\le Y\le 140.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(120.5\le Y\le 140.5) & =P(\frac{120.5-126}{\sqrt{50.4}}\le Z\le \frac{140.5-126}{\sqrt{50.4}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.77\le Z\le 2.04) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.04)-P(Z<-0.77) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.04)-P(Z\le -0.77) \\  & =Φ(2.04)-Φ(-0.77) \\  & =0.9793-0.2206 \\  & =0.7587\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(120<X\le 140)≈0.759.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.7602.$
